`nn.Linear` consumes RNG during construction: `__init__` calls `reset_parameters()`, randomly initializing weights and bias. Zeroing afterward does not undo that consumption; inserting gates between existing layers therefore changes subsequent backbone initialization. Preserve the original construction order and wrap each added gate’s construction/initialization in `with torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[]):` for CPU construction; include the relevant CUDA device when constructing there. CPU state is always restored. Also exclude gates from later random initialization passes, or isolate those passes appropriately. [Linear source](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/nn/modules/linear.py), [fork_rng documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/random.html).

Implication: restoring initialization RNG preserves subsequent random streams, including dropout, provided device RNG states, stochastic operation order and tensor shapes remain unchanged. Gates must introduce no additional random draws during forward. Identical seeds alone do not guarantee this, and identical RNG streams do not imply identical training trajectories after changing the network. A zero-weight, zero-bias sigmoid gate outputs 0.5; multiplying a NextItNet residual branch by it immediately halves that branch. For an initially unchanged residual multiplier, `2 * sigmoid(gate(x))` starts at 1. These are mathematical consequences of the proposed gate.

AdamW applies decoupled shrinkage, `b ← (1 − lr * weight_decay) * b`, to gate biases included in decayed parameter groups. Thus decay pulls nonzero sigmoid biases toward zero, corresponding to gate output 0.5 when the input contribution is zero; initially zero biases remain zero under decay alone. Put gate biases in a `weight_decay=0` group if that drift is unwanted. Parameters with `grad=None` are skipped; zero gradients still permit decay. [AdamW documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.optim.AdamW.html).
